title: How Edinburgh locals can see the Northern Lights as further sightings 'still possible'
excerpt: Some residents across Edinburgh and the Lothians were lucky enough to capture the moment on Saturday night.
content:
Isla Storie

Sun, 11 October 2026 at 11:25 am UTC

1 min read

Locals across Edinburgh and the Lothians were treated to a spectacular show on Saturday night as the Northern Lights lit up the skies.

The phenomenon known as the Aurora Borealis - caused by an increase in solar activity - was captured by residents across the region, who made the most of the rare sight. Occurrences are usually only seen in northern Scotland.

Most people reported sightings between 7.30pm and 10.30pm. To get the best picture using a phone camera, it is recommended to turn on night mode and increase the exposure to maximum.

Spotters should also look northwards, and away from bright streetlights.

The Met Office has since said sightings could continue to be possible in Scotland during clear skies until Tuesday.

In the capital, locals in the north and east of the city - including Granton, Newhaven and Portobello - captured the aurora above them. They have previously been clear from high spots including Arthur's Seat, Blackford Hill and Calton Hill.

Across the Lothians, it was visible in places including Bathgate, Linlithgow, Penicuik and Dunbar.
